metaDescription: Uhrichsville, once the clay pipe capital of the world, sits on the Utica flank in Tuscarawas County. See how that industrial land history ties to minerals.
heroLead: Uhrichsville once called itself the clay pipe capital of the world, and the same industrial-era land transactions that fed its brick and tile plants are often where the mineral reservations under nearby farmland got their start.
intro: Uhrichsville sits in Tuscarawas County, on the flank of the Utica/Point Pleasant play. The town built its economy on clay products, sewer pipe, tile, and brick, during the late 1800s and early 1900s, and land in the surrounding townships changed hands frequently to support that industry, often with mineral rights carved out along the way.

For families near Uhrichsville today, the mineral interest tied to that era is usually a small, inherited fraction rather than a large single holding, and confirming exactly what you own starts with the recorded deed.

sections.heading: Clay-era land transactions and mineral splits
paragraphs: As clay and shale extraction for the pottery and pipe industry drove demand for land near Uhrichsville, farms were bought, sold, and subdivided at a faster pace than in purely agricultural parts of the county. Oil and gas rights were sometimes reserved during these transactions even though the buyers were after surface clay deposits, not deep shale gas.

That layered history means a title search on land near Uhrichsville can turn up mineral reservations from surprisingly specific industrial transactions, which we trace through the Tuscarawas County Recorder's office.

sections.heading: Distinguishing clay and shale rights from oil and gas rights
paragraphs: It is worth noting that the near-surface clay and shale that fed Uhrichsville's pottery industry is a completely different resource from the deep Utica/Point Pleasant formation targeted by modern horizontal drilling, thousands of feet below. A deed reserving clay or coal rights does not automatically include oil and gas.

We review the exact language of your deed to confirm which rights were actually reserved and whether oil and gas was included, rather than assuming based on the era or the industry active at the time.

sections.heading: Selling an oil and gas interest near Uhrichsville
paragraphs: Once we confirm you hold an oil and gas mineral interest, we check current activity in the surrounding flank townships and put together a written offer reflecting your documented share and nearby conditions.
This process is separate from and unaffected by any historical clay or surface mining rights that may also exist on the same original tract.

faqs.question: My old deed near Uhrichsville mentions clay and shale rights. Does that include oil and gas?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Clay and near-surface shale rights are a different resource from deep Utica/Point Pleasant oil and gas rights, and older deeds sometimes only reserved one or the other. We review the exact language to confirm.

faqs.question: Is there current oil and gas activity near Uhrichsville?
faqs.answer: Tuscarawas County sits on the Utica flank, and activity varies by township. We check current state permit and production records for your specific parcel.

faqs.question: How do I know if my family's interest near Uhrichsville is oil and gas or something else?
faqs.answer: A title search reviewing the exact deed language will confirm this. We handle that research as part of any offer.
